sections.title: A Forward-Looking European Education at Exceptional Value
sections.intro: Lithuania offers international students a compelling combination of recognised European qualifications, modern teaching and a remarkably accessible cost of study set within a safe, digitally advanced Baltic environment.

items.title: Europe-wide recognition
items.desc: Degrees follow the European Higher Education Area framework, supporting smooth recognition and mobility across Europe.

items.title: Exceptional affordability
items.desc: Tuition and living costs are among the most reasonable in the euro area, allowing students to invest in their education with confidence.

items.title: Innovation-driven strengths
items.desc: Lithuania is distinguished in information technology, fintech, life sciences, engineering, business, and health sciences.

items.title: Practical career pathways
items.desc: Students holding a residence permit may work up to 40 hours alongside studies, and eligible graduates can remain to seek employment.

items.title: A European gateway
items.desc: As a member of the EU and Schengen Area, Lithuania places all of Europe within easy reach for study, travel, and international careers.

sections.title: Distinguished Institutions in Lithuania
sections.intro: The following institutions represent key destinations available to EUROPA FUSION students.

items.name: Vilnius University
items.desc: Lithuania’s leading comprehensive research university, distinguished in humanities, law, natural sciences, medicine and social sciences.

items.name: Kaunas University of Technology
items.desc: A major Baltic centre for engineering, information technology, design and business, with a strongly international student body.

items.name: Vilnius Gediminas Technical University
items.desc: Known for engineering, architecture, construction, transport and technology, with close ties to European industry.

items.name: Vytautas Magnus University
items.desc: A liberal-arts-oriented university recognised for social sciences, humanities, informatics, arts and education.

items.name: Lithuanian University of Health Sciences
items.desc: A specialist institution offering English-taught programmes in medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary and health sciences.

items.name: ISM University of Management and Economics
items.desc: An internationally oriented institution focused on business, economics, data management, finance and entrepreneurship.

items.name: Mykolas Romeris University
items.desc: Specialising in law, public governance, security, cybersecurity, social sciences and international communication.

items.name: Vilnius University of Applied Sciences
items.desc: A practice-oriented institution offering career-focused programmes in business, technology, healthcare and creative fields.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.intro: Common questions about studying and settling in Lithuania.

items.q: Can I study in Lithuania entirely in English?
items.a: Yes. Lithuanian universities and colleges offer more than 500 English-taught programmes at Bachelor’s, Master’s and doctoral level, including medicine, engineering, business, IT and the social sciences.

items.q: Do I need to speak Lithuanian?
items.a: It is not required for English-taught programmes, though basic Lithuanian is helpful in daily life and when seeking part-time work. Universities commonly offer free or low-cost introductory language courses.

items.q: How much does it cost to study in Lithuania?
items.a: Lithuania is one of Europe’s most affordable study destinations. Tuition for English-taught programmes at public universities typically ranges from about €1,500 to €6,000 per year, while medicine and dentistry range from €10,000 to €14,000. Monthly living costs commonly range from €500 to €800.

items.q: When are the intakes and deadlines?
items.a: The main intake begins in September, with a smaller intake in February at some institutions. International application deadlines often fall between April and June, and non-EU applicants should apply early to allow time for permit processing.

items.q: Do I need to take an entrance examination?
items.a: Many programmes assess applicants on academic record, motivation letter and English proficiency. Medicine and certain health and creative programmes require entrance examinations or interviews.
Universities usually accept IELTS (typically 5.5-6.5), TOEFL, or equivalent tests. Some institutions conduct their own online interview or internal assessment.

items.q: How much money must I show for the permit?
items.a: Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds for their stay. Many universities and Lithuanian migration authorities expect proof of around €7,500 for the first year, often alongside payment of the first tuition invoice.

items.q: Can I work while studying in Lithuania?
items.a: Yes! Non-EU students holding a temporary residence permit for study in Lithuania may work up to 40 hours per week during their studies.

items.q: Can I remain in Lithuania after graduating?
items.a: Eligible graduates of Lithuanian universities may apply for a temporary residence permit to seek employment or start a business, valid for up to 12 months, and then easily transition to an EU Blue Card or work permit.

items.q: Are scholarships available for international students?
items.a: Yes. Options include Lithuanian state scholarships, Erasmus+ mobility grants, and tuition fee waivers or merit discounts offered directly by individual universities.
Most universities offer on-campus student dormitories (typically €100–€250/month), which are the most economical option, alongside shared private apartments in Vilnius and Kaunas (€250–€450/month).

items.q: How does EUROPA FUSION support my application?
items.a: We assist at every stage: profile assessment, university shortlisting, SOP & CV editing, document legalization/apostille guidance, entrance prep, visa file verification, accommodation search, and pre-departure briefings.
